validity.summary: Existence, classification, and duplicate status all check out clean; two real defects were found instead, on attribution and spec (below).
validity.evidence: EXISTENCE: a 30+ year, multi-owner paper trail confirms this is a real, currently operating pipeline — FERC Docket RP95-212-000 (govinfo.gov, 1995, predecessor entities KansOk/Riverside/Kansas Natural/Kansas Pipeline, all operated by Kansas Pipeline Operating Co.), two SEC filings from two different corporate owners a decade apart (Enbridge Inc. 2002 Form F-3, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/895728/000091205702022692/a2081445zf-3.htm; Enbridge Energy Partners LP FY2008 10-K, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/880285/000119312509033100/d10k.htm, describing the Nov-2007 sale of 'our Kansas pipeline system, or KPC' for $133M), current PHMSA public-awareness filings for both Kansas and Oklahoma (pipelinesafetyinfo.com), the current operator's own site (mvpurchasing.com/kpcpipeline/), and an operator-authored EBB informational posting (gasnom.com/ip/kpc/). CLASSIFICATION: every source independently calls this an interstate natural gas transmission system — Fuel=Gas and PipelineType=transmission are both correct. DUPLICATE: P0186 is the only KPC-related row in the 45-row batch roster; no relabel/duplicate found.
validity.researcher_notes: No change recommended on Status, Fuel, PipelineType, or existence/duplicate flags.

validity.summary: EndLocation records only 'Wichita' but every independent source describes the system's actual downstream terminus as Kansas City — Wichita is a market stop mid-route, not the end of the line.
validity.evidence: Three independent sources converge on Kansas City as the true terminus, not merely Wichita: (1) current operator site mvpurchasing.com/kpcpipeline/ — 'Our interstate natural gas pipeline runs 1,129 miles from Oklahoma City to Kansas City, including through Wichita'; (2) operator-authored gasnom.com/ip/kpc/ posting and both current PHMSA filings (pipelinesafetyinfo.com Kansas + Oklahoma) — 'transports natural gas from Oklahoma and Kansas to metropolitan Wichita, Kansas City and various other interconnecting pipeline markets'; (3) Enbridge Energy Partners LP FY2008 10-K (SEC, independent of the current MVP-era operator) — states plainly KPC 'serves the Wichita, Kansas and Kansas City, Kansas markets,' pinning the state as Kansas specifically. The current PHMSA Kansas counties-of-operation list also names Wyandotte and Johnson counties, both in the Kansas City, KS metro, confirming physical reach there (alongside Sedgwick County, where Wichita sits). A 1995 FERC Order to Show Cause about this system's direct predecessor network (KansOk/Riverside/Kansas Natural/Kansas Pipeline, operated by Kansas Pipeline Operating Co.) — govinfo.gov, https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/FR-1995-06-06/html/95-13770.htm, Docket RP95-212-000 — described the network as completing 'in Kansas City, Missouri' via a FERC-authorized 2-mile Riverside segment; that document predates and never uses the 'KPC' name, so it does not pass this project's pipeline-naming citation gate and is offered here as historical background only, not as a citable ref. Every source from the current KPC/MVP era (2008 onward) specifies Kansas, not Missouri, so the recommended candidate is 'Kansas City' with EndState/Province left as the sheet's existing 'Kansas' — no state-column change proposed.
validity.researcher_notes: StartLocation=Laverne/Oklahoma and both CountryOrArea=United States cells are independently confirmed and NOT contested (see the Location [ref] fill below). Only EndLocation is disputed.

validity.summary: StartYear1=1995 is not stated by any source found, and the one document that discusses this system's origin timeline points to gas already flowing well before 1995.
validity.evidence: No source found states 1995 as an in-service/start year for KPC or its predecessors. The 1995 FERC Order to Show Cause (govinfo.gov, Docket RP95-212-000 — background only; does not name 'KPC,' see the naming-gate caveat in the attribution concern above) instead shows the predecessor network was already operating years earlier: it cites KansOk's actual 1990 transportation volumes (2.6% intrastate / 97.4% NGPA section 311 that year, per KansOk's own 1991 filing) and states the Riverside Kansas-Missouri border segment 'was authorized under NGA section 7 in 1989' (Riverside Pipeline Co., L.P., 48 FERC para. 61,309 (1989)), with two further Riverside Oklahoma-Kansas segments built in 1992. This 1990-1992 activity window contradicts a 1995 start date for the system as a whole. No single precise replacement year could be attributed with confidence given the multi-entity predecessor consolidation (KansOk + Riverside + Kansas Natural + Kansas Pipeline, later merged, sold to Enbridge in Nov 1999, and sold again to the current KPC Pipeline LLC/MVP ownership in Nov 2007) landing on one un-segmented tracker row, so no specific candidate year is proposed here — flagging only that 1995 is very likely wrong.
validity.researcher_notes: Recommend UNRESOLVED on the Start [ref] fill rather than a false REFS_ADDED confirmation of 1995 — see fills[] below.

fills.researcher_notes: Searched FERC eLibrary/govinfo.gov, both SEC filings, the current operator's site, gasnom.com, and both PHMSA filings. No source states a ProposalYear for the consolidated KPC system. The system is a multi-entity predecessor consolidation (KansOk, Riverside, Kansas Natural, Kansas Pipeline — see the 1995 FERC Order to Show Cause, govinfo.gov Docket RP95-212-000) collapsed onto one un-segmented tracker row, which precludes attributing a single proposal date. Leaving blank rather than guessing.

Same predecessor-complexity problem as ProposalYear. The 1995 FERC Order to Show Cause (govinfo.gov, Docket RP95-212-000 — does not name 'KPC,' offered as background only) documents predecessor construction/authorization activity in 1989 (Riverside's Kansas-Missouri border segment, 48 FERC para. 61,309) and 1992 (Riverside's two Oklahoma-Kansas segments), but no source ties a single ConstructionYear to the row as it is currently structured. See the related StartYear1 spec concern in validity[]. Leaving blank rather than guessing.

No source found states 1995 specifically as a start-of-service year. The 1995 FERC Order to Show Cause about this system's direct predecessor network (govinfo.gov, Docket RP95-212-000 — background only, does not name 'KPC') instead documents gas already flowing in 1990 (KansOk's cited 1990 actual transportation volumes) and a component segment authorized in 1989 — evidence that contradicts, rather than confirms, the recorded 1995 value. See the StartYear1 spec concern in validity[] for the full evidentiary detail and the reason no replacement year is proposed. This is filed as UNRESOLVED (nothing confirms 1995) rather than REFS_ADDED, since a source disagreeing on the underlying fact is not the same as agreement within rounding.

refs.note: 'Our interstate natural gas pipeline runs 1,129 miles from Oklahoma City to Kansas City, including through Wichita.' 1,129 mi = 1,817 km exactly.
Enbridge Energy Partners LP FY2008 10-K (a different, prior corporate owner, independent of the current MVP-era operator): 'approximately 1,120 miles of pipeline.'
'...a 1,120 mile interstate gas pipeline...'

fills.researcher_notes: Two genuinely independent corporate eras (Enbridge pre-2007 vs. the current MVP/KPC operator) both put the system at approximately 1,120-1,129 miles — the current operator's figure (1,129 mi) matches the sheet's 1,817 km exactly; the ~9-mile (0.8%) variance against the older 1,120-mile figure is treated as agreement within rounding per standing rule 4(e), not a discrepancy. Important scope note: this length covers the FULL system described by every source as running from the Oklahoma gathering area through Wichita to Kansas City — see the EndLocation attribution concern in validity[] for why the sheet's recorded endpoints (Laverne, OK to Wichita, KS only) understate the system's actual extent even though the length figure itself is correct.

refs.note: '...approximately 1,120 miles of pipeline ranging in diameter from 4 to 12 inches, along with three compressor stations.'

fills.researcher_notes: Only one source found (Enbridge Energy Partners LP FY2008 10-K, an SEC filing — independent of the current operator, though single-sourced). Searched the current operator's site, gasnom.com, and both PHMSA filings; none of them state a diameter figure. Tiered medium per standing rule 4 (single source) rather than left UNRESOLVED, since the source is an authoritative regulatory filing, not marketing copy.

Per docs/reference/gem_schema.md's FuelSource gotcha, this column names a specific upstream field/plant/facility, not a fuel type or a broad geological region. Every source found (gasnom.com, both PHMSA filings) says only that KPC is 'capable of distributing Anadarko and Arkoma basin gas' — these are broad multi-state geological basins, not a named field or plant on the level of the schema's own examples (Abqaiq, Hasbah Gas Field). No specific named source facility was found; leaving blank per the schema's explicit 'do not default it' instruction rather than filling with a basin name or 'Natural Gas.'

HOWEVER: see the attribution concern in validity[] — every source describes the system's actual downstream terminus as Kansas City, not Wichita, so EndLocation is separately flagged as incomplete even though 'Wichita' itself is a genuine point on the route.

Searched both SEC filings, the 1995 FERC order, and operator/PHMSA materials. Only transaction (M&A) values were found, not a construction/segment cost: Enbridge Energy Partners LP sold the system in November 2007 for $133 million in cash (net asset value ~$100.4 million, including $9.2 million of goodwill — FY2008 10-K), and Enbridge Midcoast Energy had itself acquired 'the Kansas pipeline system' in November 1999 (Enbridge Inc. 2002 Form F-3). Both are sale/acquisition prices, not a build cost, so neither is an honest fill for SegmentCost. Leaving blank.

summary: P0186 KPC Gas Pipeline: existence/classification/duplicate all confirmed clean; 9 MISSING_REF units re-cited as REFS_ADDED (Status, Fuel, PipelineType, Capacity, Length, Diameter, Location, Operator, Owner) and 6 MISSING_VALUE units resolved (Diameter filled) or left UNRESOLVED with notes (Proposal, Construction, Start, Pressure, FuelSource, SegmentCost); two validity concerns staged — an attribution concern on EndLocation (system's true terminus is Kansas City, not Wichita) and a spec concern on StartYear1 (1995 is unsupported and likely wrong per 1989-1990 predecessor evidence).
